exchanges.title: Deterministic recommendation policy is a degenerate mu, not a correlated equilibrium
exchanges.red_demand: Exhibit a concrete mu non-trivially correlated across agents, or downgrade the Aumann reframe to Nash on the conflict-graph-augmented game.
exchanges.white_counter: No white-team defense was authored against this probe; the operator's call is that the v2.6 figure (symmetric tie-break: mu draws (claim_alpha, defer_beta) with probability 1/2 and (defer_alpha, claim_beta) with probability 1/2, which is not the product of marginals at a symmetric-conflict tie) exhibits the required non-trivial correlation. WT-v25v26-005 (two-layer folk-theorem TLA+) is the formal answer for the production-extension question and is tracked as a carried artifact.
exchanges.synthesis: Closed by figure plus one-sentence binding in \S\ref{sec:correlating-device} that names the figure as the witness mu and notes that the deterministic policy of the property statement is the policy in the no-tie case; the tied case (symmetric conflicts on a single resource) is where mu has non-trivial correlation. The probe's demand (a) is met by the figure; the probe's alternative (b) -- downgrade to Nash on the augmented game -- is declined.

exchanges.synthesis: Declined. The red team's own report explicitly acknowledges the arithmetic is correct ('numerical root ~0.2534, paper rounds to 0.253'). The proposition statement already names the stage-game payoffs explicitly via Table~\ref{tab:claim-stage-game} and the 'What each condition buys' bullet on delta-star already routes the short-lived-principal regime to \S\ref{sec:economic} bond pricing. The probe asks for a more general statement of the proposition. That is a legitimate generalization but it is not a defect in the current statement -- the current statement is a concrete instance with an explicit payoff table, which is the standard way to write a folk-theorem application in a system paper. Carrying the more general form (option a or c) into a future round if a reviewer asks for it; not blocking v2.6 on it. exchanges.title: Mechanize Proposition 7.1 in TLA+ (Apalache delta-sweep) + Z3 check of the cubic
exchanges.smell_from: whitehat-defense-fleet self-audit (v2.5 ships analytic proof, no mechanization handle)
exchanges.red_demand: (no direct red probe; complementary to RT-003)
exchanges.white_counter: Two-agent repeated claim-signaling game with three-round graduated trigger as the agent's local automaton, Merkle-evidence history as shared variable, delta in {0.20, 0.25, 0.253, 0.30, 0.50, 0.90} as discrete parameter. Apalache: for delta > delta-star_{k=3}, no finite trace of length <= N admits a strictly profitable one-shot deviation from (T,T); for delta <= delta-star, Apalache produces a counter-trace at the smallest delta in the grid. Pair with Z3 SMT check of 3delta^3 + 3delta^2 + 3delta - 1 > 0 so the threshold itself is machine-checked.
exchanges.synthesis: Closed by artifact. Blocking for v2.6 because it grounds the proposition in mechanized evidence parallel to the existing \S\ref{sec:tlaplus} TLA+ citations and forms the spec into which H_anchor (from RT-007 / WT-003) is parameterized. The artifact citation lands at the end of the deviation-analysis paragraph (~line 706 of the .tex).
